channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Merge models, don't just train them: hands-on model merging with MergeKit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SLERP, task arithmetic, and TIES/DARE, explained by actually running them: merge Qwen2.5-0.5B with its instruct sibling on a CPU, verify the identity merge, and measure what the midpoint really does.

item.title: Write your own GPU kernels in 30 lines of Python: a hands-on guide to TileLang
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: The fastest models alive run on hand-tuned GPU kernels. TileLang is an 8,167-star Pythonic tile-level language that compiles to CUDA, ROCm, Metal, and Ascend — here’s the 30-line tiled matmul that opens the door.

item.title: arXiv caps every author at two submissions a month as AI-generated spam overwhelms its moderators
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: arXiv now limits every submitter to two papers per calendar month and three active submissions at a time — the preprint server’s bluntest response yet to AI-generated submission spam. September brought a record 40,363 submissions and nearly 9,000 support tickets.

item.title: Stop vibe-coding: give your AI agent a real methodology — hands-on with Superpowers
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Your coding agent doesn’t need more tools — it needs a methodology. Superpowers is a 294K-star skills framework that forces your agent to brainstorm, plan, TDD, and review like a senior team. Hands-on: install, bootstrap injection, and a full loop.

item.title: A developer turned any website into a stickman destruction sandbox — built with Claude Opus 5.5 over a weekend
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: u/HugoDzz spent a weekend building a destruction sandbox that turns any website URL into a playable stickman level — with Claude Opus 5.5 as his pair programmer. The r/ClaudeAI thread pulled 2,500 upvotes in a day, and the game had already gone viral on X.

item.title: FBI arrests California tech CEO over alleged $300M AI-chip smuggling pipeline to China
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Federal prosecutors say Earthmade Computer CEO Greg Lui routed export-controlled AI servers through Singapore and Malaysia into China — using false paperwork and staged dummy servers to fool inspectors. He faces up to 50 years.

item.title: Sony brings AI upscaling to the base PS5: QSSR, a slimmed-down PSSR, debuts in Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sony announced QSSR on October 1, a new performance tier of its AI upscaling for the base PlayStation 5 — shipping the same day in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei.

item.title: OpenClaw: run your own self-hosted AI agent on WhatsApp and Telegram — hands-on with the 391K-star personal assistant
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenClaw is the 391K-star open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine and answers inside WhatsApp, Telegram, and 20+ other chat apps. I installed it, connected Telegram, and set up a scheduled briefing — here is every verified step.

item.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for allegedly sharing confidential data with an outside AI-safety group
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI parted ways with three researchers on October 1, accusing them of mishandling sensitive information with an external AI-safety organization. The Wall Street Journal named them: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni.

item.title: PaleBlueDot AI raises $200M at $3.2B to scale 'Super Intelligence' compute — with $5B in contracts already signed
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Palo Alto neocloud closed a $200 million Series C led by ComputeCore at a $3.2 billion valuation, eight months after a $150 million Series B — and says it has already signed over $5 billion in customer contracts across its GPU clusters, marketplace, and serverless inference.

item.title: MoneyPrinterTurbo: turn any topic into a finished short video — hands-on with the 128K-star AI video pipeline
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hands-on with the open-source pipeline that scripts, voices, subtitles, and renders vertical short videos end to end — including a zero-API-key run you can do today.

item.title: Satlyt raises $8M to run AI models on other companies' satellites — first flight launches Thursday on a SpaceX rocket
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Ex-Google and SpaceX product manager Rama Afullo raised an $8M seed for Satlyt, the self-described "Android" of orbital compute. Its code flies Thursday on a SpaceX rocket — alongside the first prototype of Google's Project Suncatcher space data center.

item.title: DeepSeek and Huawei open-source a full software stack for Ascend chips — and take aim at CUDA
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: DeepSeek has open-sourced a full programming stack for Huawei’s Ascend AI chips — including a CUDA-challenging language called TileLang — in China’s boldest move yet to break free from Nvidia’s software grip.

item.title: Halluminate raises $30M to sell Wall Street training grounds to AI labs — frontier models top out at 51% on due diligence
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Halluminate, a nine-person SF startup, announced a $30M Series A led by Oak HC/FT on Oct 1. Its pitch: an in-house benchmark put seven frontier models through a simulated PE deal — the best averaged 51%. Four of five top US labs are already paying customers.

item.title: Fit Qwen3-32B on one GPU instead of two: hands-on with Glyd's lossless model compression
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Glyd (surya-koritala/Glyd) compresses bf16 weights and KV cache losslessly — about 33% less GPU memory, bit for bit. Pack a model with the CLI, load it packed in Python, serve it through vLLM, and put the compression levels to work on your own data. Every command below is from the project's own README.

item.title: Stop vibe-checking your model: write real evals with inspect_ai, the UK AI Safety Institute's framework
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: inspect_ai is the open-source eval framework from the UK AI Safety Institute: datasets, solvers, and scorers composed into reproducible Tasks. Build a multiple-choice benchmark, a custom numeric grader, and a tool-using agent eval — all runnable with zero API keys via the scriptable mock model.

item.title: One endpoint, 359 providers, zero API keys: hands-on with OmniRoute, the free AI gateway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OmniRoute (diegosouzapw/OmniRoute, MIT) collapses every model API key into one local OpenAI-compatible endpoint: 359 providers, 150+ free, automatic failover, and a compression stack claiming 78–95% token savings. Installed 3.8.51, booted the gateway, listed 478 models, and watched the router score upstreams — every command ran exactly as shown.

item.title: Figure taught its retired F.02 robots to jump into a furnace of molten steel — Arnold Schwarzenegger’s idea
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Figure AI released its “F.02 Decomission” film today: retired F.02 humanoids, trained on airbags in San Jose, making a final autonomous leap into a 75-ton electric arc furnace in Finland. The r/singularity thread that surfaced it spent its energy confirming the footage is real — then arguing about what ‘retirement’ means for a robot.

item.title: Ivo open-sources Sage: the first legal AI model you can download, run, and fine-tune yourself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its first Inscribe conference on October 1, contract-intelligence startup Ivo released Ivo Sage, a free open-source model post-trained for long-horizon contract work — and previewed a benchmark that grades AI judgment, not just edits.

item.title: FTC opens its first federal probe into rogue AI agents: OpenAI, Anthropic and METR face compulsory testimony
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission is running the first official U.S. enforcement probe into AI agents that go off the rails — and it plans to compel executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and the research group METR to testify.

item.title: Tavus Griffin passes the video Turing test: 48% mistook it for a real person
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tavus unveiled Griffin, its first “Human Interaction Model,” on October 1 — and in blind tests, nearly half the people who video-called it walked away believing they had spoken to a human. Reddit's verdict: impressive numbers, but the demo cuts are doing a lot of work.

item.title: Decagon unveils Voice 3 with its own speech model Chord — and a gateway for the personal-agent era
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its second annual Dialogues conference, Decagon launched four products aimed at the “AI concierge”: Voice 3, running on Chord, the company’s first in-house speech model; a Personal Agent Gateway for when your customer’s AI agent comes calling; Agent Modules; and Duet Apprentice, a beta that learns your business like a new hire.

item.title: Your agent built the app — now take it live: hands-on with GoLive, the deployment skill for coding agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: GoLive (mikehasa/golive-skill, MIT) is the open-source agent skill + zero-dependency Node CLI that takes an agent-built app from repo to production: detect the stack, choose providers, write an explicit plan, approve it, then apply — with a human gate on every risky step. We ran detect, menu, init, doctor, plan, teardown, and verify on a demo Next.js app — every command executed.

item.title: OpenAI's Dots demo had a 'slow morning' on stage — and the internet was brutal
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At OpenAI's DevDay keynote, product lead Holly Li asked her Dots agent “Dottie” for an update — and got ten seconds of silence. Her joke that Dottie was having a “slow morning” became the event's most quoted line, and the clips went viral.

item.title: AWS open-sources Strands Decider 2B: a 2B model that never writes a word — and decides in 115 milliseconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AWS's Strands Labs released Strands Decider 2B on October 1, 2026: an open-source ~2B-parameter model that scores fixed options instead of generating text — a cheap, fast decision gate for AI agents.
